title: Generative
description: Generative visuals show process: forms grown by rule, particles, and iteration, so cinema is made by a system rather than only by a finished photograph. Making is visible.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: A body, a city, or a cloud is not posed. It is grown.
Cells, grains, or agents iterate until a figure appears. Use it when the point is how the image becomes, not only what it depicts.
It is the wrong tool for a codec wound or a person turning into a beast. If the look is smashed motion vectors, you want datamosh.
If a body becomes another body in continuous view, you want a transformation.

sections.title: How it works

blocks.text: Treat the forming matter as something you can light. Name the rule (particles, iteration, grown geometry), the scale of the bits, and a hard or soft source that rakes them.
The camera can be locked so the growth is the move. Keep a readable subject so the system has an object.
Prompt a generative image of the subject: forms grown by rule, particles, and iteration, cinema made by a system.

sections.title: When to use it

blocks.text: Use it for the beat when a world or a face is still assembling. Do not use it as a style wash on a finished portrait that never needed a rule.

sections.title: Compared with similar shots

blocks.text: Datamosh is deliberate compression failure: I-frames gone, motion vectors smeared. Generative growth is a rule, not a wound in the file.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousins are Datamosh and a generic melt. The tell is blocky codec smear, or a face liquefying with no rule.
The fix is named iteration, countable bits, and a subject the system is growing toward.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is generative in film?
Generative visuals show process rather than only a finished result. Forms are grown by rule, particles, and iteration, so the system that makes the picture is visible.
Generative vs datamosh
Datamosh breaks the file on purpose. Generative work builds an image by iteration. One is a codec artifact. The other is a rule you can light.
When should I use generative?
Use it when becoming-by-rule is the scene: a city assembling, a body grown from particles. Skip it as a filter on a still that is already complete.
How do I prompt generative for AI image or video?
Write Generative image of [Subject], forms grown by rule, particles, and iteration. Name the rule, the scale of the bits, and the light. Keep a readable end state.
